He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best [[shooting guard]]s in the 2020 class. He finished his high school career at [[Whitney M. Young Magnet High School]] in [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]]. ==High school career== Steward first attended [[Fenwick High School (Oak Park, Illinois)|Fenwick High School]] in [[Oak Park, Illinois]].{{cite web|title=DJ Steward - 2020-21 - Men's Basketball|url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dj-steward/16344|work=Duke University|access-date=July 11, 2020}} In 2018, he transferred to [[Whitney M. Young Gifted & Talented Leadership Academy|Whitney Young High School]] in [[Chicago]], Illinois for his remaining years of high school.{{cite web|title=D J Steward, 2020 Shooting Guard, Duke|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/d-j-steward-205660|website=Rivals.com|date=September 18, 2019|access-date=October 17, 2024}} Steward averaged 24.1 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game in the 2019 Nike EYBL circuit. In the Highland Shootout versus [[Christian Brothers College High School]] in January 2020, Steward scored a shootout-high 40 points including the game-tying bucket in a 66–64 victory. He was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]].{{cite news|first=Michael|last=O'Brien|title=The streak is over: Young's DJ Steward is a McDonald's All-American|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2020/1/23/21078824/dj-steward-mcdonalds-all-american-high-school-basketball|work=[[Chicago Sun Times]]|date=January 23, 2020|access-date=July 24, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== On September 18, 2019, Steward committed to play at [[Duke University]]. He chose the Blue Devils over offers from [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]], [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]].{{cite magazine|first=Alaa|last=Abdeldaiem|title=Five-Star guard DJ Steward commits to Duke|url=https://www.si.com/college/2019/09/18/dj-steward-commits-duke|work=Sports Illustrated|date=September 18, 2019|access-date=July 11, 2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = DJ Steward | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Chicago, IL]] | highschool = [[Whitney M. Young Magnet High School|Whitney Young]] (IL) | feet = 6 | inches = 3 | weight = 165 | 40 = | commitdate = September 18, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 92 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = Duke 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 Duke Blue Devils Recruiting Class | rivals school = duke | scout s = | espn schoolid = 150 | 247 overall = 23 | rivals overall = 29 | espn overall = 25 | accessdate = July 25, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Steward started 22 games and played in 24 games during Duke's 2020–21 season. A {{convert|6|ft|2|in|adj=on}} combo guard, he averaged 13 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game.{{cite news|first=John|last=Watson|title=Former Blue Devil DJ Steward Cut By Sacramento|url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/Article/Former-Blue-Devil-DJ-Steward-Cut-By-Sacramento-173115687/|work=247 Sports|date=October 17, 2021|access-date=October 17, 2021}} The Duke team finished that season 13–11, with a 9–9 record in the ACC. It was the first year since 1995 that the Blue Devils were not invited to the NCAA tournament. While the season did not live up to Duke's usual expectations, Steward had multiple highlights during his only year on the team. In his college debut on November 28, 2020, Steward scored 24 points in an 81–71 win against [[2020–21 Coppin State Eagles men's basketball team|Coppin State]].{{cite news|title=Johnson, Steward help No. 9 Duke beat Coppin State 81-71|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401259835|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 28, 2020|access-date=November 28, 2020}} On December 21, 2020, Steward was named [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] rookie of the week.{{cite web|title=Syracuse's Guerrier, Duke's Steward Notch ACC Men's Basketball Weekly Honors|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/12/21/syracuses-guerrier-dukes-steward-notch-acc-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx|website=TheACC.com|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|date=December 21, 2020|access-date=December 21, 2020}} On January 15, 2021, Steward scored 26 points and grabbed 6 rebounds in a 79–68 win over [[2020–21 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]].{{cite web|title=No.21 Duke tops Wake Forest 79–68 in Krzyzewski's return|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401260206|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 15, 2021|access-date=January 15, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Stockton Kings (2021–2023)=== After a very successful freshman season at Duke, Steward debated going professional. At {{convert|6|ft|2|in}}, Steward was seen as having a shooting guard's skills in a point guard's body, and this led to a sense that he would need to develop point guard skills before he could effectively play in the NBA. Nevertheless, he decided to make himself available for the NBA draft. After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Steward was invited to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|first=A.|last=Singh|title=Kings Announce California Classic Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-2021-ca-classic-roster|website=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2021|access-date=October 3, 2021}} On September 28, 2021, he signed a contract with the Kings.{{cite web|title=Kings Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=September 28, 2021|access-date=September 28, 2021}} He was waived prior to the start of the season. Steward signed with the [[Stockton Kings]] of the [[NBA G League]] as an affiliate player for the 2021–22 season.{{cite web|title=Stockton Kings Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}} ===Vancouver Bandits (2023)=== On April 6, 2023, Steward signed with the [[Vancouver Bandits]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=Vancouver Bandits Sign Former Duke Starter, Stockton Kings Star Guard DJ Steward for the 2023 CEBL Season|url=https://www.cebl.ca/vancouver-bandits-sign-former-duke-starter-stockton-kings-star-guard-dj-steward-for-the-2023-cebl-season|website=CEBL.com|date=April 6, 2023|access-date=April 7, 2023|archive-date=April 6, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406214251/https://www.cebl.ca/vancouver-bandits-sign-former-duke-starter-stockton-kings-star-guard-dj-steward-for-the-2023-cebl-season|url-status=dead}} He was released by the Bandits on June 5 in order to prepare for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]], where he would play for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=Vancouver Bandits Release Trio of || 22 || 30.8 || .426 || .341 || .811 || 4.0 || 2.4 || 1.1 || .6 || 13.0 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Steward is the son of Katicha Jackson-Williams and [[Danny Boy (singer)|Danny Boy Steward]], and stepson of [[Tyrone Hill]]. He is named after his father, who was a former [[Death Row Records|Death Row]] recording artist. He also played football in high school, and has a brother, Trent. Steward grew up in Oak Park, Illinois where he attended Brooks Middle School. He attended Fenwick his freshman and sophomore years, then transferred to Whitney Young for his last two years. He played travel ball since his middle school years with Meanstreets and played EYBL circuit, where he made an even bigger name for himself.{{cite web|title=Brooks wins 2nd annual village tourney|url=https://www.oakpark.com/2015/01/13/brooks-wins-2nd-annual-village-tourney|website=OakPark.com|date=January 13, 2015|access-date=October 19, 2023}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/dj-steward/16344 Duke Blue Devils bio] *[https://web.archive.org/web/20200613084528/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/s/steward-dj.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{CB Miraflores current roster}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Steward, DJ}} [[Category:2001 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century African-American sportsmen]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Canada]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Italy]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Aquila Basket Trento players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Chicago]] [[Category:Duke Blue Devils men's basketball players]] [[Category:Maine Celtics players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Memphis Hustle players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Stockton Kings players]] [[Category:Vancouver Bandits players]] [[Category:Windy City Bulls players]]
